Base64Bytes.description: Bytes as standard-alphabet base64 with `=` padding.

Clock.description: The clock the frame times of a stream were taken from: an object whose `kind` is `monotonic`, with an `anchor`, or `unrecorded`, which has no frame times.

oneOf.description: Frame times are nanoseconds of a monotonic clock, anchored to one wall-clock reading.

anchor.description: The wall-clock reading and the monotonic reading taken together.

oneOf.description: The stream was framed after the fact and its frames have no times.

ClockAnchor.description: One wall-clock reading paired with the monotonic clock at the same moment.

mono_ns.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
mono_ns.description: The monotonic clock in nanoseconds at that reading.

wall.description: The wall-clock reading, an RFC 3339 timestamp.

Digest.description: A content digest: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits.

FrameData.description: The content of one frame: an object whose `kind` is `text`, with valid UTF-8 under `text`, or `bytes`, with standard base64 under `base64`.

oneOf.description: The frame's bytes are valid UTF-8, written as text.
The frame's bytes are not valid UTF-8, written as base64.

base64.description: The frame's bytes in standard base64 with padding.

StreamName.description: The name of an archived stream: `stdout`, `stderr`, or the name of a collected file, matching `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*`.

Timestamp.$comment: The pattern states the lexical form; a date or time that names no instant, such as month 13, and a fraction of more than nine digits are refused by the parser.
Timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp with an uppercase `T` and an explicit offset, `Z` or `±HH:MM`.

description: One line of a raw frame file: an object whose `kind` is `header` or `frame`.

oneOf.description: The first line of the file.

clock.description: The clock of the frame times.

source.description: The digest of the file the frames were cut from, when they were cut after the fact.

stream.description: The name of the archived stream.

t_mono_ns.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
t_mono_ns.description: The monotonic time of the frame in nanoseconds; absent when the clock is unrecorded.
